title: macOS: sign and notarize the release app so Gatekeeper opens it without a workaround

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

body:
### What are you trying to do

Open CamCraft on a Mac after downloading it from the releases page, without having to override Gatekeeper.

The macOS app is ad-hoc signed and not notarized (`scripts/package-macos.sh`: "Distribution signing and notarization can replace this when credentials exist"). A browser download gets the quarantine flag, and macOS then blocks the first launch because Apple can't verify the developer. Every new release is a new copy, so a user has to override Gatekeeper again after each update.

The README says the first launch "may require Control-click → Open". Since macOS 15 (Sequoia) that no longer works for an app that isn't notarized: the user has to try to open it, then go to System Settings › Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway, or run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/CamCraft.app` in Terminal.

### How you imagine it working

The release signs the macOS app with a Developer ID certificate and notarizes it, so it opens like any other downloaded app. It would work the same way Windows signing does now (`scripts/sign.ps1`):

- `scripts/package-macos.sh` signs with Developer ID (hardened runtime, secure timestamp) when signing credentials are configured through the environment, and keeps today's ad-hoc signature, with a printed "unsigned" line, when they aren't. Unsigned stays a valid release.
- When credentials are configured, the release job submits the ZIP or DMG with `xcrun notarytool submit --wait`, then staples the ticket to the app and the DMG with `xcrun stapler staple`.
- The certificate and the notary credentials (an App Store Connect API key, or an Apple ID with an app-specific password) live in repository secrets, as the Windows PFX does.

This needs an Apple Developer Program membership, so whether and when to do it is the maintainer's call. A smaller step that helps meanwhile: update the README's macOS line to the macOS 15 steps above.
